messages.subject: RW(1) model
parts:
Hi guys,

I have a question about the structure of the RW(1) model in INLA. 

The code of rw(1) in INLA is: 
f(id, model="rw1")

On the website of INLA, it says the RW(1) is: 
x[i] = x[i-1] + e, e~N(0, sigma2)

While in the paper of "Spatial and patio-temporal models with R-INLA", on page 7, it says the 


with seemly the same rw(1) code.

Does anyone know what is the difference of these two cases? When we write the f(id, model ="rw1"), which structure is used?

Thanks
Blangiardo, Marta, et al. "Spatial and spatio-temporal models with R-INLA." Spatial and spatio-temporal epidemiology 7 (2013): 39-55.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] RW(1) model
parts:
The two formulation describe the same model. The one in the book gives the full conditional distributions, I.e. when conditioning on both the past and future. The formulation you quote from the website is the sequential, timeseries, formulation, where conditioning is only on the past.

Finn

On Wed, 2017-05-03 at 06:35 +0100, Finn Lindgren wrote:
> The two formulation describe the same model. The one in the book
> gives the full conditional distributions, I.e. when conditioning on
> both the past and future. The formulation you quote from the website
> is the sequential, timeseries, formulation, where conditioning is
> only on the past.

INLA also accepts irregular locations both for RW1 and RW2, and that
case is discussed in the GMRF-book for RW1, and for RW2 in a paper by
Finn in Scandinavian Journal of statistics.
